documents.title: Dataset Construction and DQ Assessment – Residential Real Estate Mortgages

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
sections.text: This document describes the construction of the reference data set (RDS) for the PD-MORT-NL v4 model and the assessment of its data quality. It follows the RDS template of MRM-STD-021 and was approved by the Head of Retail Credit Risk Modelling on 12 June 2027 (document version 1.0).

sections.heading: Observation period
sections.text: The reference data set covers monthly snapshots from January 2012 to December 2024, totalling 9.6 million account-months for 780,000 unique facilities.

sections.heading: Choice of observation window
sections.text: The window was chosen to maximise the available history after the migration to the current mortgage administration system in 2011. It includes the 2012–2013 housing market downturn and the low-default period 2016–2021.

sections.heading: Default definition
sections.text: A facility is flagged as defaulted when it is more than 90 days past due above a materiality threshold of EUR 100 absolute and 1% relative, or when an unlikeliness-to-pay trigger is met.

sections.heading: Unlikeliness-to-pay triggers
sections.text: UTP triggers comprise distressed restructuring, forced sale of the collateral, bankruptcy of the obligor and specific credit risk adjustments. Triggers are sourced from the arrears management system and applied at obligor level.

sections.heading: Data sources and lineage
sections.text: All 38 candidate variables are sourced from the mortgage administration system, the arrears management system and the collateral valuation database. Lineage from source table to RDS field is documented in Annex A for every variable.

sections.heading: Exclusions
sections.text: Loans with incomplete collateral information were excluded from the RDS (3,412 facilities, 0.4% of the population; 61 defaults). Facilities originated under the former brand portfolio were excluded (1,208 facilities, 0.15%; 9 defaults) because origination data is unavailable. The combined exclusions affect the long-run default rate by +0.01pp.

sections.heading: Missing values and outliers
sections.text: Missing values for debt-to-income at origination (2.3%) are imputed with the segment median; outliers in indexed LTV above 250% are capped. Both treatments are justified in Annex C.

sections.heading: Representativeness
sections.text: Population stability between the RDS and the current portfolio was assessed using the PSI on loan-to-value bucket, loan age and interest-only share (PSI 0.04–0.06). Annex B adds a comparison of the full LTV distribution.

sections.heading: Impact of exclusions
sections.text: Excluded loans show a comparable LTV distribution to retained loans (PSI 0.03) and a comparable default rate (0.47% vs 0.45%); the exclusions are therefore not expected to affect representativeness.

sections.heading: Data quality assessment
sections.text: Completeness and accuracy were assessed for all 38 variables using the DQ rules of MRM-STD-022. Consistency was checked across the three source systems. All critical data elements pass the thresholds.

sections.heading: Data deficiencies
sections.text: The default flag for 2012–2015 was approximated from arrears data prior to the implementation of the new definition of default. Probation periods could not be reconstructed for this period.

sections.heading: Personal data and fair treatment
sections.text: The RDS contains personal data processed under the legal obligation of the CRR; a DPIA was completed (DPIA-2026-118). Nationality and gender are excluded. Postcode was assessed as a potential proxy and is only used at regional level within the house-price index.

sections.heading: Reproducibility
sections.text: The RDS is built by versioned code in repository rds-mort-nl (tag v4.0.0). A full rebuild reproduces the RDS row count and default count exactly.

sections.heading: Margin of Conservatism
sections.text: The approximation of the default flag for 2012–2015 is treated as a category A data deficiency. A MoC of +6% relative is applied to the long-run average default rate.
